author: wsfa12news
title: Montgomery shooting leaves man injured
text:
A Sunday morning shooting in Montgomery, Alabama, has left a man injured. The incident occurred in the early hours of the day, and while details are still emerging, the victim sustained non-life-threatening injuries and was transported to a local hospital for treatment.
One local realtor says despite rate hikes, it's still a good time to buy if the payment fits your budget. Mullins has sold homes in the River Region for more than twenty years.
"When I bought my first house in the late 90s, it went from 10 to 9. So, I got single digits. I thought I'd won the lottery. So, we're not really in high rates," said Mullins.
He says today's mortgage rates feel high only because buyers got used to unusually low, rock‑bottom rates in the early 2000's. But rates began to rise during the pandemic.
"Unfortunately, the COVID era, the low rates, they put us in a position where some people just, you know, don't want to give up that rate and I don't blame them," said Mullins. Mullins says national headlines about "rate hikes" can sound scary, but sometimes the change represents just one‑tenth of a percent, which has little impact on a monthly payment.
"Find the house you love. That's where you want to be. You know, the rate is going to be what it is. It's going to be tight.
As long as you can afford it comfortably and make sure that payment is going to be comfortable for what you can afford and live; Don't worry about the rate," said Mullins. According to Mullins, inventory around the River Region is healthy, and many sellers, including builders, are offering concessions and rate buy‑downs to help buyers get to a payment they can live with.
For renters who dream of owning, Mullins urges them to sit down with a local lender and see the numbers for themselves. Sunday morning Montgomery shooting leaves man injure
